title: Eat Well, Sleep Well, Move Well
summary: The three habits that keep your body and mind strong.

steps.title: A balanced plate
sentences: Our body needs carbohydrates for energy, proteins to grow and repair, fats in small amounts and vitamins and minerals to stay healthy.
A good plate has grains, pulses or eggs or milk, vegetables and fruits.
Drinking enough water helps every part of the body.

steps.title: Eat the rainbow
sentences: Different coloured fruits and vegetables give different vitamins.
Try something green, something orange and something red each day.
Sweets, chips and fizzy drinks are fine now and then, but they should not replace real meals.

steps.title: Move your body
sentences: Children should get about an hour of active play every day.
Running, cycling, skipping and sports make your heart, bones and muscles stronger.
Moving also helps you feel happier and think better.

steps.title: Sleep
sentences: While you sleep your body grows and your brain stores what you learned.
Try to go to bed at the same time every day and put screens away an hour before sleep.
Wash your hands before meals and brush your teeth twice a day.

facts: Your bones stop growing taller in your late teens but keep renewing all your life.
Millets such as ragi and kambu are rich in minerals and have been eaten in Tamil Nadu for centuries.
Laughing and playing with friends are good for health too.

quiz.q: About how much active play should children get daily?
quiz.why: Experts suggest about 60 minutes a day.

quiz.q: What helps your body grow and repair?
quiz.why: Proteins help build and repair the body.
